utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning. Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber has decided that we are going to a Status Conference because we have problems with the trial proceedings, to proceed right away. We can see that Mr. Milan Simic is not here. There are problems with his transportation and the services that are required for him to be brought to the Trial Chamber. The Trial Chamber wanted to find out from the Defence counsel for Mr. Milan Simic -- we had decided on Friday that we would sit late if the nurse and the other services required for him were available for the witnesses that discuss his involvement. We wanted to find out from them whether, on cross-examination, if it is not possible to have him in the courtroom, if he stays at the detention centre with the video-like facilities being provided for him to follow the proceedings while at the detention centre, whether that would be acceptable.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, we are really happy to discuss this. As a matter of fact, we have been trying to work something out with the Registry the last couple of weeks to try to move things along and come up with some solution to make this trial go by faster. We are happy to have our client sit in the jail every day, and we can sit here in trial as many hours as the Trial Chamber sees fit, but only -- the defendant only wants to absent himself from this trial if there are witnesses that are not dealing with his case. In other words, if the Prosecution will stipulate that on those days where he's sitting in the jail, that those witnesses will not be used as evidence against him, then that is great with us and we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, no. That is a bit not clear, when you say "those witnesses will not be used as evidence against him." That's different from having a witness discussing direct involvement of the accused.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I understand, but, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because, if you see, the whole indictment, there are specific charges against Mr. Milan Simic. Now, other witnesses may be discussing other things other than the direct involvement of Mr. Milan Simic.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's the difference.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I understand. But not only the United States and Serbia and other European countries, the most important thing is that the defendant be present for his trial, and the defendant cannot be tried in absentia unless he volunteers. It's the defendant's right to make the decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Are you saying that if arrangements were made, like we do teleconferences, he's in the detention centre, he's following the proceedings, every facility is there for him to follow the proceedings, save for the physical presence in the courtroom --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that's what I'm saying. I'm not exactly sure I understand what you're saying. What our client has said - and we've discussed this with him - is that he is happy to sit in the jail - in fact, he wants to sit in the jail - as long as he can be here for the witnesses who are going to be used against him, to prove the cases against him. But as far as these other witnesses -- he wants to be here in the courtroom to see the witness, to judge the credibility, just like the Trial Chamber, if those witnesses are going to be used as evidence against him. So this is what we've been discussing for two weeks --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because you have to be remember that we do have videolink proceedings in this Tribunal --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, and I know that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- and the issues of credibility are just as well handled by the Trial Chamber and the parties --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- because you are able to see --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And I'm aware that videolinks are used here, but the videolinks have been used for witnesses, not for the defendants. The defendant is the one who has the absolute right to be present for his trial, unless he says, "No, it's okay, I don't want to be there." Otherwise what we could do is just videotape all the witnesses, videotape their cross, and just have a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: -- give the videotapes to the Appeals Chamber, have a trial de novo there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. Let's be sensible. Let's be practical. For the witnesses directly involving Milan Simic, it's understandable. He has to be present. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: For those witnesses who are not discussing his direct involvement, he can stay in the Detention Centre, follow the proceedings on video.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, as long as we have a stipulation from the OTP that they will not use that evidence to prove his guilt. That's perfect. That's absolutely what we want to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. That's a twist. Because it's the whole indictment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we can't get our client to agree not to be here for those unless we have a stipulation. That's the problem. It's the client's decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no. You explain to the client what the difficulties are, and it's a question of being reasonable, because if the witnesses are not discussing his direct involvement but they're discussing the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I totally understand your point, Your Honour. I just -- we haven't gotten there with our client yet. We haven't got him to agree to that yet. That's the problem. When we signed up for this, we thought the Prosecution was going to be done with their case by the end of November, so that's what happened at Pre-Trial Conference. That's what the Judges said: This will be done -- the OTP will be done by November. So we're just as anxious to move this along as you are, Your Honour, or maybe just -- almost as anxious as you are. So we're trying -- we really are trying to work with the Registry to move things forward, but we can't get our client to agree to sit over there if they are going to be using some of these witnesses against him to prove the different allegations in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Let me hear from the Prosecution. MR. DI FAZIO: Well, I -- the position of the Prosecution, if Your Honours please, is that naturally we are very keen to proceed with this videolink proposal because, of course, I think it would expedite the trial and cut down the amount of time that we're spending and give us more working hours in the day. As far as the general principle is concerned, of course Mr. Simic has an absolute right to be at his trial, and the Prosecution does not seek to do anything to interfere with that. But insofar as a stipulation is concerned - and I understand that to mean undertaking or guarantee or assurance or something like that - is concerned, we cannot provide any guarantee or undertaking or stipulation that the witness's -- the evidence of a witness will not be used against Mr. Milan Simic, and we simply will not do that. However, the Prosecution can and will use its best efforts to identify any witness who can give direct evidence, in the sense of evidence touching upon the personal actions of Mr. Milan Simic, well in advance to the Defence. That would mean that Mr. Milan Simic would be present at all times when any witness is speaking directly about his actions. Now, for the remainder of the evidence, it will be, as far as he's concerned, general background evidence, evidence of the persecutions and labour, forced labour, and so on. For the remainder of that evidence, if there's a videolink, and if, furthermore, there is some means of communication between Mr. Simic in his cell - or wherever it is in the prison that he is - and counsel in the courtroom, then I can see absolutely no prejudice to him whatsoever. Everything that he wants to do can be done, because if he sees something or observes something or wishes to communicate with his counsel, he picks up the telephone or whatever the communication device is - I don't know about the technology - and simply rings Mr. Zecevic or Ms. Baen and says, "Make a note of this or that." So in practical terms, I think it's an ideal and a fine solution, and I would heartily commend it to the Defence and to the Chamber. The Prosecution will do whatever it can to facilitate that arrangement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because if I mention something -- because you can't -- the Prosecution can't make that undertaking, because you can't determine what a witness will say. MR. DI FAZIO: Not in advance, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, in the witness box. MR. DI FAZIO: I understand that. I understand that. Naturally, we can't provide a cast-iron guarantee, but we can do a pretty good job of predicting if a witness is going to speak of the direct actions of Mr. Milan Simic and put them on notice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think -- yes. The other question is -- because we can't decide that now. We have to wait and see whether a nurse will be available. The other question is: The witnesses available this week, is it only the two of them, Mr. Salkic and Mr. Tihic? MR. DI FAZIO: Well, that's all we've made arrangements for. Now there are some witnesses who live in nearby countries, Belgium and Germany.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because the other suggestion would be: Because these two witnesses have other matters they have to attend to, it may be necessary to adjourn both of them off until next year, both of them. MR. DI FAZIO: May I respectfully ask why?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The reason is we are already losing time and we may not finish, definitely not both of them. The cross-examination may not finish, because we may not be able to have Mr. Milan Simic in the courtroom for the long hours. MR. DI FAZIO: Oh, for the long hours, but we -- the hours that we've been keeping up until Friday will continue this week, won't they?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Subject to the facilities being available. I mean, like now we haven't got a nurse, and it's not possible to have a replacement nurse right away. MR. DI FAZIO: I see. I think I misunderstand the situation. I thought this was just a hiccup this morning, just a minor problem this morning, or is this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, because -- MR. DI FAZIO: Is this going to be ongoing for the entire week?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Tribunal does not control the provision of the nurse. It's another company, we are informed. So the nurse who usually looks after him in the morning was involved in an accident. Yes. So it may not be possible to have a replacement right away. MR. DI FAZIO: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The possibility is that perhaps this afternoon. Yes, because this is the problem now. We may not finish the cross-examination of both. MR. DI FAZIO: I understand. I'm sorry. I didn't quite have a grip on the situation. May I just confer briefly with my colleagues, if Your Honours please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. If Your Honours please, if that's the case, and it looks like there is going to be problems this week with hours, then the Prosecution's preference is that we would -- of the two witnesses, we would prefer to forge ahead with Mr. Tihic. Now, he's not arriving until tonight apparently. He's driving over from Bosnia. I think he's driving via Germany, and he's going to be here tonight. That's the arrangements that have been made. Now, he is on his way. It's not a flight, and in terms of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If all facilities were available, and he will be here, we will start with him in the morning on Tuesday. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: 9.30. MR. DI FAZIO: That's the expectation. We could, yes. It wasn't expected that he would start precisely tomorrow morning because we thought do Mr. Salkic today and perhaps part of tomorrow and then start Tihic and, God willing, finish him by the end of the week. That was what I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We all thought that would be possible, but we can't control the provision of services, which is the problem. MR. DI FAZIO: I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It wouldn't be nice to have a witness start cross-examination and then cut them off in the middle of that and then have them to come next year. It's easier to break between examination-in-chief and cross-examination. MR. DI FAZIO: Far easier. And that other course that you just mentioned is not one that the Prosecution would be happy with, I'm sure the Defence wouldn't be happy with, and I'm sure it makes it harder for Your Honours to follow the evidence if we are chopping and changing from topic to topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe what we can do right now is adjourn until we are informed whether or not it's possible to have Mr. Simic this morning. Otherwise, if he can't come before 11.30, then we will start the proceedings at 1400 hours. Hopefully, the lunch-hour nurse hopefully may agree to go and collect him. If he can't come before 11.30, then we sit at 1400 hours, hopefully with Mr. Milan Simic in, and continue with Mr. Salkic, you finalise examination-in-chief, we go on to cross-examination, and perhaps sit up to 18.30. MR. DI FAZIO: Anything that can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think it's better to have specific hours, rather than just keep waiting, because in the meantime the Prosecution can look at the list of their witnesses and start working out those which may not touch Mr. Milan Simic, and we start -- at least we use the time usefully when we know we are expected in court at such and such an hour, and also Defence counsel can be preparing what they have to prepare. MR. DI FAZIO: We can do that, and we can come up with a plan B, so to speak, in the event that disaster strikes completely and we really grind to a halt. But that won't be a problem. We can do that. We can arrange other witnesses for later in the week, if necessary, but as I said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I do hope that the Defence counsel also appreciate that it's much better, once you start cross-examination, to finish, rather than do it halfway, in case we don't have the facilities for Mr. Milan Simic another day during the week.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: By all means, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So it may be the situation may be that both Mr. Salkic and Mr. Tihic may not be heard this week. We may have them next year so that we can accommodate the problems we are facing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We understand the unfortunate situation, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. So we will adjourn and wait until 11.30. If Mr. Milan Simic can't be here, then we will sit at 1400 hours. MR. DI FAZIO: I take it if he's not turned up just before 11.30, if the parties ascertain from court staff that he's not going to be here, there is no need to reconvene.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. MR. DI FAZIO: We just won't sit until 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Court will rise.
